name: Pinterest
look: Masonry pin grid on warm-cream chrome, one red CTA, a two-radius shape system and a sticky always-red sign-up.

hero.title: Get your next idea from someone who tried it
hero.sub: Save what you like, group it into boards, and get recommendations from four hundred million people saving the same kind of thing.

features.title: Save it now, find it later
features.sub: A visual bookmark that actually resurfaces when you need it.

items.title: Save anything
items.body: From the app or from any website with the browser button. The original link comes with it, always.

items.title: Boards
items.body: Group saves by room, trip or project, with sections inside a board once it gets unwieldy.

items.title: Visual search
items.body: Circle part of an image and find that chair, that tile, that plant — not the whole photo again.

items.title: Shared boards
items.body: Invite people to add to a board. Useful for a kitchen renovation, dangerous for a wedding.

items.title: Recommendations
items.body: Based on what you save rather than what you linger on, so the feed stays about your actual project.

items.title: Links that work
items.body: Every pin keeps its source. If a link rots, we say so rather than quietly showing a dead end.

showcases.title: Find the chair, not the room
showcases.body: Circle any part of an image and search on that region alone. It is the difference between finding the same photograph again and finding the thing inside it you actually wanted.
points: Search a selected region, not the whole image
Works on your own saves and on the web
Shows the source and where to buy it

showcases.title: People arrive already deciding
showcases.body: Someone saving kitchen tiles is nine months from a renovation and already choosing. Product pins carry live price and stock, and click through to your site rather than keeping the customer here.
points: Live price and stock on product pins
Clicks go to your site, not an in-app checkout
Attribution over a longer window than social

gallery.title: Explore
gallery.sub: A slice of what people are saving this week.

testimonial.quote: I planned an entire kitchen renovation on one shared board with my partner and the fitter. Eleven months of decisions, and every one of them still links back to where it came from.
testimonial.name: Hannah Okonkwo

pricing.title: Moodboard for business
pricing.sub: Free to publish. You pay only if you advertise.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.desc: Publish pins and see how they perform.

tiers.name: Ads
tiers.desc: Promote pins to people already searching.

items.a: Yes, entirely, for personal use and for publishing as a business. The only thing you pay for is advertising, and that is optional.
No. Advertising is targeted on what you search and save on Moodboard, not on data bought from elsewhere. Personalisation can be turned off in settings.

items.q: What happens when a link breaks?
items.a: The pin is marked as having a broken source rather than silently linking nowhere, and it stops being recommended in the feed.

items.q: Can I make a board private?
items.a: Yes — a secret board is visible only to you and anyone you explicitly invite, and it never appears in search or recommendations.

cta.title: Start your first board
cta.sub: Free forever, and everything you save keeps its original source.

footer.tagline: A visual bookmark that resurfaces when you need it.

notes: The masonry pin grid is the load-bearing visual element. Each pin keeps its natural aspect ratio; forcing a uniform crop destroys the whole system.
One red carries every primary action. Everything else in the chrome is monochrome on warm cream.
Two radii do all the work: 16px for most components, 32px for large cards and modals, plus full circles for avatars and icon buttons.
The chrome is warm cream (#f6f6f3), chosen to recede behind imagery rather than compete with it. Pure white would fight the pins.
The sign-up CTA is red and anchored top-right at every breakpoint. It never moves and it never changes colour.
